name: F/A-18C/D Hornet
summary: Original-generation twin-engine Hornet, now flown in US service only by a dwindling number of Marine Corps squadrons as they convert to the F-35.

wings: Mid-mounted trapezoidal wing with a straight leading edge (no dogtooth)
Long slender leading-edge root extensions (LERX) with small fences on top
engines: Two engines with round exhausts side by side
Rounded D-shaped intakes tucked under the LERX
fuselage: Slim fuselage with pointed nose and bubble canopy
D model has a two-seat tandem cockpit
Smaller and slimmer than the Super Hornet
tail: Twin outward-canted vertical fins mounted well forward of the exhausts

tellTales: Rounded D-shaped intakes under long slender wing-root extensions
Small twin canted fins set well forward of the exhausts
Little fences standing up on top of the wing-root extensions

confusedWith.howToTell: The legacy Hornet is smaller with rounded intakes and a straight wing leading edge; the Super Hornet has rectangular intakes, a wing dogtooth and bigger LERX.
The Hornet has two engines and twin canted fins with intakes on both sides; the F-16 has one engine, one fin and a single chin intake.
The Hornet's canted fins are mounted forward of the exhausts and its intakes are under the LERX; the F-15 has upright fins at the very tail and large box intakes.

usCount.source: Marine Corps Times / USMC Aviation Plan (legacy Hornet phase-out)
